subtype: Shy, embarrassed and ashamed in adult settings [Regulating]
passage: In Gothenburg, Oskar mixed up two client names in front of the whole department, and someone laughed. His face flushed, and for the rest of the meeting he spoke only when asked. At lunch he took his sandwich to a quiet corner. Sofia, from the next desk, sat down anyway and said, "Last month I called the CEO by the wrong first name. In an email." Oskar blinked and gave a small smile. She added, "Tomorrow, would you like to go over the next slide together before the call?" He nodded slowly. The next day he said just one line in the meeting, about the deadline, and his voice shook only slightly. It was a small step. By Friday he had asked a question.

qa.q: What was Oskar feeling for the rest of the meeting?
qa.a: Embarrassed and ashamed, since his face flushed and he spoke only when asked.
Speaking one line the next day, after preparing with Sofia.

qa.q: How might Sofia's story about the wrong first name help Oskar?
qa.a: It shows that public mistakes happen to others too, so his feels more ordinary. 🙂

grounding: A young adult withdraws after a public mistake, and a supportive colleague treats it as ordinary and helps him take small steps.

subtype: Shy, embarrassed and ashamed in adult settings [Regulating]
passage: At the cricket club's Sunday nets, Pooja dropped an easy catch in the practice match while the whole club watched. Someone groaned. Her ears burned, and she turned away and spent the second half fielding at the boundary, far from everyone. In the changing room she said she might skip next week. Vasudha, the senior player, sat down and said, "Everyone drops the easy ones. I dropped one in a league match last year, in front of my parents." She didn't tell Pooja not to feel bad. She asked, "Want to do ten catches with me before nets next week? Just us." Pooja hesitated, then nodded. The next Sunday, after catching seven of ten, she asked to stand at slip.

qa.q: Where did Pooja field in the second half?
qa.a: At the boundary, far from everyone.

qa.q: What was Pooja feeling after she dropped the catch?
qa.a: Embarrassed and ashamed, since her ears burned, she pulled away and she considered skipping next week.

qa.q: How did Vasudha help Pooja return?
qa.a: She shared her own dropped catch, offered private practice and a small step.

qa.q: How might the club see the dropped catch?
qa.a: As an ordinary slip, since Vasudha says everyone drops the easy ones; the groan was probably a passing reaction.

grounding: A young adult withdraws after a public mistake at a club, and a supportive senior treats it as ordinary and offers a small private step.
